newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin returns to work in Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin returns to work in Kremlin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin returned to work in the Kremlin on Monday, almost seven weeks after major heart surgery.
The president's motorcade rolled through the Kremlin's Borovitsky Gate soon after 9.30 a.m. (0630 GMT).
"I am feeling fine," Yeltsin told a television crew inside the Kremlin administration building, adding that he was looking forward to starting his duties.
He said his priorities would include dealing with delays in paying pensions and wages and the need for military reform.
"The coming year will be better for Russia. That is the firm word of the president," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying.
Yeltsin had a quintuple heart bypass on November 5 and has been recuperating since then in hospital and government rest houses.
He moved to an official residence near Moscow on Sunday ready for his trip back to the Kremlin.
The president, speaking in his first television address since the operation, said on Friday that Russia needed an active president, new ideas and courage, and he promised an energetic return to work.
Yeltsin, 65, looked much thinner than before his surgery and he spoke in a firm and decisive voice.
But he appeared somewhat stiff and distant, lacking the spark which he displayed during his campaign for re-election in the first half of this year.
